items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: they had a trumpet player named Willie Jackson; we had a pianist named Martha Davis... Mr. Robinson's son, Mundy -- he was the same age I was -- he played drums and I played the fiddle.

ctx.x: How did you cope with your studies with all this music? I mean, you were in school.

I was in school, and I don't know -- they knew that a few of us in the school was playing around, you know; we had a piano player, Horace Parnum, and I took my fiddle to school one day for assembly, and we played. That was just before I got out of grade school to go to Wendell Phillips. I would have little jobs, and Well, I would tell my teacher that I had to go and play -- this wasn't much later; I'd say about '38. No, it wasn't quite '38 -- '37. I was working with a band at that time. Mr. Robinson had a club…

she had a duo -- Martha Davis Davidson and spouse -- a beautiful pianist. And, Mr. Robinson's son, Mundy -- he was the same age I was -- he played drums and I played the fiddle. Mr. Robinson bought me a fiddle -- I think he paid $75 for it, and he said every week, I'd have to pay him so much until I paid for it myself.
